from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Uncertainty Principle: The Duality of Time and Frequency",
            ["Fourier transforms decompose signals into frequencies.",
             "A pure sine wave has infinite duration.",
             "A sharp click has perfect time localization."]
        )

        # Objects
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE)
        pulse = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 1.0 * np.exp(-10 * t**2), x_range=[-1, 1], color=RED)
        tuning_fork = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tuningfork.svg")
        drumstick = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drumstick.svg")
        
        # Grid positioning
        self.place_in_area(sine_wave, 'B3', 'B5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(pulse, 'E3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(tuning_fork, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(drumstick, 'E2', scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sine_wave), FadeIn(pulse), FadeIn(tuning_fork), FadeIn(drumstick))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(sine_wave.animate.stretch(1.5, dim=0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(pulse.animate.stretch(0.2, dim=0))
        self.wait(2)

        ])

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Precise frequency requires long signal cycles.",
            "Truncating signals causes spectral leakage.",
            "Trade-offs exist in phase information."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Why Can't We Have Both? The Phase Interference", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        osc1 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/oscillator.svg")

        # Animations

        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Bat's Echolocation", [
            "Bats balance time and frequency resolution.",
            "Short clicks aid distance detection.",
            "Frequency sweeps help identify prey."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        bat = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bat.svg")
        target = Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        combined_group = VGroup(bat, target)
        
        # Layout
        self.place_at_grid(bat, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(target, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(combined_group, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.75)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        # Emit frequency-modulated chirp
        chirp = VGroup(*[Line(bat.get_right(), bat.get_right()+RIGHT*0.5, color=RED) for _ in range(3)])
        chirp.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(chirp), chirp.animate.shift(RIGHT*2))
        self.play(FadeOut(chirp))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        # Show echo returning
        pulse = Dot(color=RED).move_to(bat.get_right())
        self.play(pulse.animate.move_to(target.get_center()))
        self.play(pulse.animate.move_to(bat.get_center()))
        self.play(FadeOut(pulse))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Illustrate time-of-flight / sweep
        sweep = VMobject(color=YELLOW)
        sweep.set_points_smoothly([bat.get_right(), bat.get_right()+RIGHT*1.5+UP*0.5, bat.get_right()+RIGHT*2+DOWN*0.5])
        self.play(Create(sweep))
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep))

outline.topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Duality of Time and Frequency
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in engineering, physics, or mathematics

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Musical Note vs. The Drum Beat
sections.content: Establish the prerequisite: The Fourier Transform decomposes a signal into its constituent frequencies. Introduce the trade-off: A pure, infinite sine wave provides perfect frequency information but zero time localization, while a short, sharp 'click' provides perfect time localization but spreads across all frequencies.
sections.example: Visualize a long, smooth flute note (constant pitch) versus a sharp, sudden snap of fingers (no identifiable pitch).

sections.title: Defining the Trade-off: Mathematical Visualization
sections.content: Introduce the standard deviation (spread) in time (Δt) and frequency (Δω). Present the mathematical inequality: Δt * Δω ≥ 1/2. Use a visual 'container' analogy: if you squeeze the pulse in the time domain, it must bulge in the frequency domain to compensate.
sections.example: An animation of a Gaussian pulse: as the bell curve narrows on the time-axis (horizontal), it automatically broadens on the frequency-axis (vertical).

sections.title: Why Can't We Have Both? The Phase Interference
sections.content: Explain that the Fourier Transform relies on global phase synchronization. To define a precise frequency, you need many cycles. If you truncate the signal (to locate it in time), you lose the phase information required to resolve the frequency, leading to spectral leakage.
sections.example: A 'Chirp' signal (a frequency that slides) demonstrating that we can only measure frequency accurately if we allow the signal enough time to unfold.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Bat's Echolocation
sections.content: Apply the concept to a biological context. Discuss how a bat must balance time resolution (to avoid hitting a tree) and frequency resolution (to distinguish between different types of insects). Explain that biological evolution optimizes this tradeoff.
sections.example: A bat emitting a short 'click' to detect distance (high time precision) and a long 'frequency-modulated sweep' to identify prey texture (high frequency precision).

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
sections.content: Recap that this is a fundamental property of wave motion, not a limitation of our sensors. Conclude that the Uncertainty Principle is the 'tax' we pay when we try to observe the world through waves.
sections.example: A final visual summary: a 'slider' on a digital dashboard that allows the student to adjust the width of a window, watching the spectral resolution degrade as temporal precision improves.
